items.details: Pick up rental car at Cancun Airport, drive 2 hours to Chiquila. Park car (100 pesos / $5 per 24h). Ferry to Isla Holbox every half hour, ~200 pesos ($10) adult.

items.details: Recommended luxury stay on Holbox; she stayed here on her first trip. Beachfront area, pool, romantic room design, outstanding food.

items.name: Cabo Catoche boat trip

items.details: Popular boat trip to Bird Island, uninhabited Pasion Island (sandbar walk), and Cenote Yalahau on the mainland.
items.name: Three-island boat trip

items.details: Available June through September; peak season July and August. Called one of the coolest activities in Mexico.
items.name: Swim with whale sharks

items.details: Popular sunset spot on Holbox for cocktails at sunset.

items.details: Recommended breakfast stop on the mainland in Chiquila before driving on.

items.details: Ferry back to Chiquila, pick up car, drive just over 2 hours to Valladolid, crossing from Quintana Roo into Yucatan state (1 hour time change).

items.details: Luxury pick in Valladolid; described as possibly the most beautiful property in town with chic colorful rooms, outdoor hammocks and pool.
items.name: Le Muuch Hotel

items.name: Casa Tia Micha

items.name: Hotel Zazil-Maj

items.name: Chichen Itza

items.details: Cenote right in downtown Valladolid with waterfalls; one of the deepest cenotes in the region; recently reopened after renovations.
items.name: Cenote Zaci

items.details: Gelato cafe in Valladolid; hard-to-find good gelato in Mexico, limited but inventive flavors (she loved the rosemary).

items.details: Cafe on Calzada de los Frailes; she had a great pay de limon (lemon pie) here.
items.name: ConKafecito

items.details: Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Old City early before the heat; hire a local guide (Dubrovnik Tourist Board office outside Pile Gate) or get lost on your own through hidden pathways and staircases.
items.name: Explore Dubrovnik Old Town

items.details: Pass covering City Walls access, small museums/galleries (she liked the Franciscan Monastery), free public transport and discounts. Summer 2025 pricing: 40 EUR ($44) 1-day, 50 EUR ($55) 3-day, 60 EUR ($66) 7-day.
items.name: Dubrovnik Pass

items.details: Her favorite restaurant in Dubrovnik since 2014; Michelin-recommended seafood. Known for tartares, pasta with shrimp and Istrian truffles, and fish cooked in a crust of salt.
items.name: Proto

items.details: Capon (castrated rooster) specialist in the Old City, open Mar 15 - Nov 15; alternative for non-seafood eaters. Capon truffle gnocchi was one of the best things she ate in Dubrovnik.
items.name: Kopun

items.details: Cable car to the top of Mount Srd; go about an hour before sunset for the best colors. Round trip 27 EUR ($28) adults, 7 EUR ($7) children 4-12.
items.name: Dubrovnik Cable Car

items.details: Dinner atop Mount Srd with panoramic views; surprisingly great food. Tip: call and book a table with the best view at least a month ahead. Open mid March to mid November.
items.name: Panorama Restaurant

items.details: Wine bar in the Old City run by an Australian man and Croatian wife; great place to try Croatian wines by the glass (Dingac reds from Peljesac; Grk and Posip whites from Korcula).
items.name: D'Vino Wine Bar

items.details: Morning sea kayak around the Old City with views of the Old Town; tours from $43 USD including a snorkeling break on a secluded beach; solo kayak rentals also available. Lokrum Island is a possible longer option.
items.name: Sea kayaking around the Old City

items.details: Her three beach picks: City Beach (adjacent to Old City), Pasjaca Beach (35-min drive south, most beautiful but rugged path), Sveti Jakov Beach (8-min drive south, locals' favorite). No private beaches in Croatia - all are public.
items.name: Beach morning options

items.details: Walk the walls ~2 hours before closing to avoid midday heat. High season 40 EUR ($42) adults; low season 15 EUR ($16). About two hours, one-way counterclockwise.
items.name: Walk the City Walls at sunset

items.details: Her lunch recommendations in the Old Town: Kamenice (mussels fresh from the sea), Bota Sare Oyster and Sushi Bar (oysters and sushi), Pizzeria Castro (pizza, heard good things), Dolce Vita (gelato, bitter orange + dark chocolate).
items.name: Lunch spots: Kamenice, Bota Sare, Pizzeria Castro, Dolce Vita

items.details: Traditional Croatian peka dinner (octopus or lamb/veal cooked under the bell with potatoes over coals) hosted by locals Marija and Zlatko in their backyard, with cured meats, cheeses, liqueurs and local wine. Book via Dubrovnik Eat With Locals; ~$100 USD per person.
items.name: Peka dinner with Marija & Zlatko

items.details: Morning visit to the island next to Dubrovnik (City of Qarth in Game of Thrones); rock slab beaches, botanical gardens, Benedictine monastery, Iron Throne at the free visitor center. Ferry 7 EUR ($7) each way, 15 min, up to 25x daily in peak season. Half day recommended.
items.name: Visit Lokrum Island

items.details: Day trip to her favorite quiet Croatian island: dense forest, neon-blue saltwater lakes; rent a bike in Mljet National Park, hike 45 min to Montokuc viewpoint, swim in saltwater lakes, visit the monastery on St. Mary's Island. Early morning ferry to Polace (90 min, 10 EUR each way). Lunch: pizza and beer at Pizzeria Levanat in Pomena.
items.name: Mljet Island day trip
items.price_hint: Ferry 10 EUR ($10) each way to Polace

items.details: Interactive museum of Croatia's communist/Yugoslavia era near the Gruz ferry port; 90 minutes is enough. Entry 9 EUR ($9) adults.
items.name: Red History Museum

items.details: Dubrovnik was King's Landing; a mainland tour covers most filming sites in 2-3 hours. A Viator tour is linked; check whether Lokrum Island is included (most mainland tours skip it).
items.name: Game of Thrones tour

itineraries.summary: Kate's three-day Dubrovnik itinerary paces Old Town exploration, beach/pool downtime and sunset experiences instead of racing through sights. Day 1 covers the Old City, lunch at her favorite restaurant Proto, the cable car to Mount Srd and dinner at Panorama; Day 2 is sea kayaking, beaches, the City Walls at sunset and a traditional peka feast with locals; Day 3 offers Lokrum Island, Mljet Island, the Red History Museum or a Game of Thrones tour.

items.details: Stayed two nights, but they say one day is enough: world's largest statue of Lenin's head, main walking street, a church near the end of the walking street, a monastery on a hill overlooking the city, and another monastery 45 minutes outside the city.
items.name: Ulan-Ude sightseeing

items.details: Final leg: another 64 hours of non-stop train travel to Vladivostok. They found no interesting stops between Ulan-Ude and Vladivostok.
items.name: Train: Ulan-Ude to Vladivostok

items.details: End of the railway journey; they note their Vladivostok time was cut short by their onward flight needs and would have spent more time there.
items.name: Vladivostok stopover

items.details: Three-step visa process for US passport holders: letter of invitation (they got one via Fortuna Travel for $12 after VisaHQ quoted $50/person for the letter), visa application (delivered in person to a Russian consulate or via visa service), and visa registration within 7 working days in Russia.
items.name: Russian visa logistics (pre-trip)

items.details: Locals in Moscow recommended stopping in Kazan (predominantly Muslim city); they also recommend booking a stop in Yekaterinburg (where the last tsar was executed) for those interested in Russian history.
items.name: Suggested additional stops: Kazan and Yekaterinburg

itineraries.summary: Kara and Nate's own 11-day (they state '10 days and 11 nights' in the route section) Trans-Siberian journey covering 9,280 km: Moscow to Irkutsk (74h non-stop train), 2 nights Irkutsk (Lake Baikal gateway), 6.5h train to Ulan-Ude, 2 nights Ulan-Ude, then 64h non-stop train to Vladivostok. 7 nights slept on the train, 2 nights in a hostel, 2 nights in a hotel. The post is a full practical guide (Russian visa steps, route choice, ticket buying) plus what they'd do differently. Day numbering here is approximate (derived from leg durations in the source) - the post is leg-structured, not day-numbered.
itineraries.title: The Ultimate Guide to Riding the Trans-Siberian Railway (Moscow to Vladivostok)

Assessment: @latinamericatravel ("Latin America Travel", ~298K Instagram followers, listed as a regional cultural/adventure travel account) is a brand/thematic account, not an individual creator, and no original itinerary content attributable to it was found. Web searches for the handle plus itinerary/guide keywords returned only unrelated tour-operator itineraries (Wanderlust, Journeys International, Enchanting Travels, Totally Latin America) and YouTube videos by other creators that merely use #latinamericatravel as a hashtag - none of that content belongs to this handle and none was extracted. The account's Instagram profile page itself could not be fetched (Instagram requires login), and no bio-link website, blog, or guides page for this handle surfaced in search. Recommend treating this handle as a repost/aggregator account in the pilot.
